beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The familiar promise of trustlessness therefore becomes a more precise investigation of relocated trust.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This is where the earlier design grammar proves useful again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers can inspect a technical innovation without confusing automation with legitimate authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Plural currencies need ways to meet, but greater connection is not automatically greater resilience.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An exchange route can broaden access while transmitting a failure across previously separate systems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book compares different monetary worlds under stress rather than imagining frictionless universal conversion.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Some boundaries protect local purposes or limit the spread of losses.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Others exclude users or make a network dependent on a powerful intermediary.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The distinction requires examining actual obligations, not merely counting available connections.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These chapters deepen the reading promise from design vocabulary into institutional consequences.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The final futures are scenarios for comparison, rather than a forecast of inevitable fragmentation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Personal agents might help people navigate many specialized claims and payment rules.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That convenience could also concentrate decisions inside another interface users barely understand.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book keeps asking who governs admission, conversion, surveillance, correction, and exit.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its constitutional language treats money as rules for living together across time.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Technology enlarges possible arrangements without choosing a fair arrangement on our behalf.
